verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA's crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II will mark the first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit... crewed lunar flyby'; R2: 'The Artemis II test flight will be NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R6: 'to orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R9: 'Crewed Lunar Flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe Artemis II as NASA's first crewed mission involving a lunar flyby/orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day journey'; R3: '10-day mission'; R4: '10-day trip'; R5: '10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission'; R9: 'MISSION DURATION 9 Days, 1 Hour, 32 Minutes'; R10: 'approximately 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: All references consistently state approximately 10 days.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'April 1 between 6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET'; R3: 'blasted off... on Wednesday evening' (April 1, 2026); R9: 'LaunchED April 1, 2026'; R10: 'lifted off... at 6:35 p.m. EDT Wednesday' (April 1, 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of exact date in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida at Launch Complex 39B'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R10: 'Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify Kennedy Space Center, FL.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II consists of Reid Wiseman (NASA), Victor Glover (NASA), Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA - Canadian Space Agency).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman... pilot Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen... Canadian Space Agency'; R2: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen'; exact matches in others
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list and agencies confirmed across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II validates the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA will test life support, communications, and navigation systems'; R10: 'demonstrate life support systems for the first time with crew'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports testing/validation of life-support systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft with a crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'demonstrate that the Space Launch System (SLS)... and the Orion crew capsule... can meet the mission objectives'; R2: 'first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R10: 'first crewed flight of this rocket and spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first crewed test of SLS and Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed lunar flyby since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit in more than 50 years. The last mission to do so was Apollo 17 in 1972'; R3: 'first crewed lunar flyby in 50 Years'; exact phrasing in title

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will travel around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fly by the far side of the moon (passing between 4,000 and 6,000 miles above it)'; R3: 'passing over the far side'; R11: 'path around its far side'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm flyby of far side.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will break records for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'set a distance record for the farthest that any humans have traveled from Earth: 252,799 miles'; R5: 'could travel farther from Earth than any human ever has, breaking the Apollo program’s distance record'

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests critical systems including the Universal Waste Management System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test critical spacecraft systems'; R3/R4: Universal Waste Management System is key system first used/tested on mission, with post-launch troubleshooting
verifications.reasoning: Mission tests critical systems; toilet (UWMS) is explicitly a new critical system first deployed.

verifications.claim: The Universal Waste Management System reportedly experienced a minor fault light shortly after launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'blinking fault light... controller issue... shortly after launch'; R4: 'glitch... blinking fault light... Within hours of launching'; R8: 'blinking fault light... controller issue'
verifications.reasoning: Direct reports of fault light post-launch.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will conduct organ-on-a-chip studies to analyze radiation impacts on health.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Using “organ-on-a-chip” devices, the astronauts will study the impact on increased radiation and microgravity on crew health'; R5: 'AVATAR experiment... organ-on-a-chip devices to measure the impacts of radiation and microgravity on human health'
verifications.reasoning: Exact description of organ-on-a-chip for radiation/health.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will deploy four international satellites.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Deployment of four international CubeSats satellites from Argentina, Germany, Korea and Saudi Arabia'; R3: 'Four small satellites called CubeSats... will soon be deployed'; R5/R10 similar
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed deployment of four international CubeSats.

verifications.claim: Artemis I was an uncrewed flight in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uncrewed Artemis I test flight in 2022'; R2: 'uncrewed Artemis I in 2022'; R7: 'In 2022, Artemis I marked the first... uncrewed'

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'builds on the success of the uncrewed Artemis I in 2022'
verifications.reasoning: Directly called successful; implied in others as foundational.

verifications.claim: Artemis III lunar landing is planned.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III was originally planned... but NASA changed the plan and it will now be a crewed rendezvous mission... Artemis IV through V... will land astronauts on the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Source explicitly states Artemis III no longer a lunar landing; changed to rendezvous mission.
